name: Pidgin Hindustani
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Siegel, Jeff. 1990. Pidgin Hindustani in Fiji (Glottolog med 319690); APiCS survey ch. 70 (read: phonology section covers segments only, no stress statement).

sources.citation: Siegel, Jeff. 2013. Pidgin Hindustani structure dataset. In Michaelis et al. (eds), Atlas of Pidgin and Creole Language Structures Online, ch. 70 (feature value comments and IPA text). Leipzig: MPI-EVA.
sources.note: APiCS has no word-stress feature, but the glossed/IPA text example for language 70 might carry stress marks; not checked.

sources.citation: Siegel, Jeff. 2013. Pidgin Hindustani. In Michaelis, Maurer, Haspelmath & Huber (eds), The Survey of Pidgin and Creole Languages, vol. III. Oxford: OUP. = APiCS Online survey chapter 70 (web edition,https://apics-online.info/surveys/70), sec. 4 Phonology.
sources.note: Silent on stress. Sec. 4 gives vowel and consonant tables only: 'The phonology of Pidgin Hindustani represented here is that of Fijian speakers. It is similar to that of Fijian, except that the voiced stops are not prenasalized, and there is no distinction in vowel length.' Only prosodic remark in the chapter: 'Yes/no questions are indicated by intonation.'

sources.citation: Siegel, Jeff. 1992. Language change and culture change among Fiji Indians. In Dutton (ed.), Culture change, language change: case studies from Melanesia, 91-113. Pacific Linguistics C-120. Sec. 4.1.3 Pidgin Hindustani.
sources.note: Sociohistorical summary of PH (verb morphology reduction); no phonology, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Siegel, Jeff. 1985. Plantation languages in Fiji. PhD thesis, Australian National University (hdl 1885/133340). Ch. 8 'Plantation Pidgin Hindustani', sec. 8.1.3 Phonology (thesis pp. 187-189), sec. 8.2.3.1 Phonology (South Indians' PH), sec. 11.3 Current Pidgin Hindustani.
sources.note: Nothing on stress placement. Sec. 8.1.3 lists segmental differences between PH (as spoken by Fijians/Chinese) and Fiji Hindustani (loss of aspiration, retroflex > alveolar, h-loss, five Fijian vowels); the only mention of stress is incidental: 'FH "long vowels" ī and ū are closest to the Fijian ones in stressed syllables and therefore are written as such' (p.188-189). No stress rule anywhere in the PH chapters (whole-file a full-text search for stress/accent/intonation confirms).

sources.citation: Moag, Rodney F. 1977. Fiji Hindi: a basic course and reference grammar. Canberra: ANU Press. p.110 (note on 'pidgin Hindi' spoken by Fijians).
sources.note: Lists four features of pidgin Hindi (-o verb ending, 'Hindi sounds are quite distorted', baiTho for hai, no politeness forms); nothing on stress in the pidgin.

sources.citation: Siegel, Jeff. 1990. Pidgin Hindustani in Fiji. In J.H.C.S. Davidson (ed.), Pacific island languages: essays in honour of G.B. Milner, 173-196. London: SOAS / Honolulu: University of Hawaii Press.
